correctness.rationale: Exact minimum-solution characterization is proved via connected edge domination of K_n. All jumps either preserve support and replace a fundamental-cycle edge, counted by \(W(F)-(m-1)\), or replace a leaf by the omitted vertex, counted by (m-1)ell(F). Prüfer leaf frequencies and tree-split Wiener sums give the exact edge census. Star/path and double-broom computations close regularity, including \(m=8\); the common-center star exchange path proves connectivity. Actual CHECK.py enumerated 33,864 original line-graph subsets for \(3\le n\le6\); every optimum, degree and global edge count passed, with supplementary algebraic shape checks.

originality.rationale: The known triangular-graph minimum connected domination number and enumeration (OEIS A373395) are excluded from the claimed novelty. The 2022 survey discusses CDS token-jump reconfiguration, mainly parameterized complexity, not local solution degree, global exchange counts, regularity or a Wiener/leaf decomposition. Prior records about spanning-tree polytope geometry and Wiener energy concern different maps and cannot imply the exact degree of minimum connected dominating solutions. No covering statement was found in actual indexed scientific/primary searches. Unindexed fixed-support tree-exchange work remains a genuine residual risk.
residual_risks: The original 2019 full article was not materially inspected; only its public abstract and the comprehensive 2022 survey treatment of its main theorems were read.

A specialized basis-exchange or tree-graph paper might formulate the same full-support-changing degrees and edge census without the words connected domination; indexed search does not eliminate this priority possibility.
No independent third-party theorem validation was performed.

value.rationale: The local Wiener-plus-leaf law resolves an all-optimal-solution reconfiguration statistic, quantifies structural flexibility in internal edge swaps versus changed omitted vertices, and yields a closed labeled all-edge census. Connectedness and the \(n\in\{3,4\}\)-only regularity boundary, including the exceptional equal star/path degree at \(n=9\) resolved by double brooms, provide new structural consequences. These are not mere re-statements of the known count of minimum sets.
